h1. Motivation

The Loki Operator currently generates a single ConfigMap ({{<lokistack-name>-config}}) containing the complete Loki configuration for all components, which is mounted by all Loki pods.

When the user makes changes to the LokiStack, the operator:

# regenerates the ConfigMap with updated content,
# computes a hash of the entire config,
# updates the pod template annotation,
# annotation change is detected and a rolling restart of all pods is triggered

The issue is that all components are restarted even if the change was irrelevant to it, this is especially problematic in the case of ingestion disruption.

* Reduce ingester restarts when non-ingester related fields change
* Leverage runtime-config’s hot reload feature
* Maintain configuration consistency

h1. Non-Goals

* Eliminating all ingester restarts

* Upstream loki changes

h4. Description of problem: 

The OpenShift Logging Operator (v6) hardcodes terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10 for collector (Vector) pods. In environments with high log volume and deliveryMode: AtLeastOnce enabled, Vector uses a disk buffer to ensure data persistence. During shutdown (SIGTERM), Vector must flush in-memory events to the disk buffer and close connections to remote sinks (like Splunk, which has a default 60s timeout). Because 10 seconds is insufficient for these operations under load, Kubernetes sends a SIGKILL while a write operation is in progress. This results in a corrupted disk buffer, causing the pod to fail its next startup.

h4. Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

* OpenShift Container Platform 4.18.30
* OpenShift Logging 6.2.9
* Vector-based collector

h4. How reproducible: 

Highly reproducible in production clusters with high log throughput (e.g., Master node Audit logs) or clusters with remote sinks experiencing intermittent latency.

h4. Steps to Reproduce:

# Configure a ClusterLogForwarder output with tuning.deliveryMode: AtLeastOnce.
# Generate a high volume of log traffic to ensure the disk buffer is active.
# Trigger a restart of the collector pods (e.g., oc rollout restart ds/instance2 -n openshift-logging or a node reboot).
# Observe the pod termination process in the node's Kubelet logs or via oc get pods timing.
# Wait for the pod to attempt a restart.

h4. Actual results:


The collector pod enters a CrashLoopBackOff state. Pod logs show: ERROR vector::topology::builder: Configuration error. error=Sink "audit-tc-splunk-hec": error occurred when building buffer: failed to build individual stage 0: failed to seek to position where reader left off: failed to decoded record: InvalidProtobufPayload

h4. Expected results:


The collector pod should be granted a sufficient grace period (e.g., 60–120 seconds) to complete its flush and shut down gracefully without corrupting the on-disk state. terminationGracePeriodSeconds should be exposed as a configurable parameter in the ClusterLogForwarder CR

h4. Additional info:

This issue is the root cause behind many "corrupted buffer" reports. While LOG-9468 introduces "self-healing" to allow Vector to skip corrupted records at startup, it does not prevent the corruption itself. Increasing CPU limits (e.g., to 2000m) is a partial workaround by allowing Vector to "flush faster," but it does not address the underlying timeout mismatch between Kubernetes (10s) and Vector's sink requirements (60s).

h4. Additional info:

For the initial research, it seems that the issue could be related to the updated AWS SDK Library. [https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/3de9d464aba7081469ffcc30c584aaf2ca061428/pkg/storage/chunk/client/aws/s3_storage_client.go#L522|https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/3de9d464aba7081469ffcc30c584aaf2ca061428/pkg/storage/chunk/client/aws/s3_storage_client.go#L522|smart-link] . With the migration, the AWS SDK v2 S3 for {{PutObject}}, the SDK could automatically adds a checksum signing with:

{noformat}x-amz-content-sha256: STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER{noformat}

Many S3-Compatible backends only accept {{UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD}} and reject that header. This is reported in upstream in - [https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/21624|https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/21624|smart-link] 

A workaround seems to be available in [https://github.com/canonical/loki-operators/pull/121|https://github.com/canonical/loki-operators/pull/121|smart-link] , but this is not possible to do in the Red Hat Loki in {{Managed}} status. 

And the definitive fix is merge in upstream in [https://github.com/canonical/loki-operators/pull/121|https://github.com/canonical/loki-operators/pull/121|smart-link] 

h3. Workaround

The workaround could be to downgrade the Loki Operator to a version before of 6.4.6 as it could be Loki 6.4.5.  

The steps for downgrade the Loki Operator can be the same detailed in [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7138224|https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7138224|smart-link]  changing the versions from the article to downgrade to Loki 6.4.5

h2. Problem

When an invalid or expired Splunk HEC token is configured in the ClusterLogForwarder output secret, the collector (Vector) pods silently drop 100% of log events with zero errors or warnings in the pod logs. The CLF status continues to report {{Ready: True}} with {{ValidationSuccess}}. This creates a *silent data loss* scenario where an administrator has absolutely no indication from the OpenShift side that log forwarding has completely failed.

The Splunk HEC endpoint correctly rejects every event with HTTP 403 and responds with {{{"text":"Invalid token","code":4}}}, but Vector at the default {{VECTOR_LOG=warn}} level does not surface these rejections anywhere.

h2. Contrast with other output failure modes

* *Splunk + Invalid URL (wrong port):* {{ERROR vector::topology::builder: msg="Healthcheck timed out."}} -- Diagnosable
* *Elasticsearch + Wrong version 6 against ES 8.x:* Continuous HTTP 400 errors logged -- Diagnosable
* *Syslog + Invalid severity keyword:* {{WARN: Invalid syslog severity value}} -- Diagnosable
* *Splunk + Invalid HEC token (HTTP 403):* Complete silence. 2 startup lines only. -- *NOT Diagnosable*

h2. Real-world scenarios where HEC tokens become invalid

* Token rotation on the Splunk side without updating the Kubernetes Secret
* Token revocation or deletion by a Splunk administrator
* Environment mismatch (dev token used against production Splunk)
* External secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) sync failures
* Copy-paste errors or truncation when creating the Secret

h2. Version-Release number

Red Hat OpenShift Logging 6.x (tested on 6.6)

h2. How reproducible

Always (100%)

h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Deploy a working Splunk HEC endpoint and configure a ClusterLogForwarder to forward application logs to it. Verify logs are flowing to Splunk successfully.

# Create a Kubernetes Secret with an incorrect HEC token:

{noformat}oc create secret generic vector-splunk-bad-secret \
  -n openshift-logging \
  --from-literal=hecToken=bad-token-value{noformat}

# Patch the CLF to use the bad secret:

{noformat}oc patch clusterlogforwarder splunk-collector -n openshift-logging \
  --type merge -p '{
    "spec": {
      "outputs": [{
        "name": "splunk-index",
        "type": "splunk",
        "splunk": {
          "authentication": {
            "token": {
              "key": "hecToken",
              "secretName": "vector-splunk-bad-secret"
            }
          },
          "url": "http://splunk-default-service.splunk-aosqe.svc:8088"
        }
      }]
    }
  }'{noformat}

# Wait for collector pods to restart (~30 seconds):

{noformat}oc get pods -n openshift-logging | grep splunk-collector{noformat}

# Manually verify that Splunk is rejecting with HTTP 403 from inside a collector pod:

{noformat}oc exec -n openshift-logging <splunk-collector-pod> -- \
  curl -s -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n" \
  -X POST http://splunk-default-service.splunk-aosqe.svc:8088/services/collector/event \
  -H "Authorization: Splunk bad-token-value" \
  -d '{"event":"test"}'{noformat}

Output:

{noformat}{"text":"Invalid token","code":4}
HTTP_CODE:403{noformat}

# Check collector pod logs:

{noformat}oc logs -n openshift-logging <splunk-collector-pod>{noformat}

# Check CLF status:

{noformat}oc get clusterlogforwarder splunk-collector -n openshift-logging \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}' | python3 -m json.tool{noformat}

h2. Actual Results

Collector pod logs show *only* startup messages after 3+ minutes of running:

{noformat}Creating the directory used for persisting Vector state /var/lib/vector/openshift-logging/splunk-collector
Starting Vector process...{noformat}

Total lines: *2*. Zero ERROR, zero WARN.

CLF status shows:

{noformat}[
  {"status": "True", "type": "observability.openshift.io/Authorized", "reason": "ClusterRolesExist"},
  {"status": "True", "type": "observability.openshift.io/Valid", "reason": "ValidationSuccess"},
  {"status": "True", "type": "Ready", "reason": "ReconciliationComplete"}
]{noformat}

*100% of logs are silently lost* with no way to diagnose from the cluster side.

h2. Expected Results

* Collector pods should log ERROR or WARN messages when Splunk HEC returns HTTP 403 (or any non-2xx response code)
* Vector healthcheck should detect an invalid token at startup and log a clear error (similar to how invalid URL produces {{ERROR: Healthcheck timed out}})
* Ideally, CLF status conditions should reflect the runtime forwarding failure

h2. Root Cause Analysis

Two layers contribute to this issue:

*1. Vector healthcheck does not validate the HEC token:*

Vector's Splunk HEC sink healthcheck uses the {{/services/collector/health/1.0}} endpoint. This endpoint checks whether HEC is enabled on Splunk, but does not validate the authentication token. So the healthcheck passes even with an invalid token, unlike the invalid-URL case which correctly triggers a healthcheck timeout.

*2. Vector does not log HTTP 403 responses at warn level:*

The generated Vector config sets {{VECTOR_LOG=warn}}. At this level, Vector's {{splunk_hec_logs}} sink silently consumes HTTP 403 responses from the event submission endpoint without logging any error or warning. The HTTP error handling that produces {{WARN vector::internal_events::http_client: HTTP error}} (seen in LOG-8302 for connection-closed errors) does not trigger for HTTP 403 responses.

h2. Potential Fix

*Option A (CLO fix -- recommended):* Modify the Cluster Logging Operator to generate a healthcheck configuration for the Splunk HEC sink that sends a test event to the {{/services/collector/event}} endpoint (instead of the health endpoint) to validate both connectivity AND token authentication at startup.

*Option B (Vector upstream):* File an upstream issue against vectordotdev/vector to ensure the {{splunk_hec_logs}} sink logs HTTP 4xx responses (especially 403) at {{warn}} or {{error}} level, consistent with how other HTTP errors (connection-closed, timeout) are already logged.

*Option C (Combined):* Implement both options for defense-in-depth -- healthcheck catches it at startup, and runtime logging catches it if a token is revoked while the pod is running.

Before this update, the generated VRL transform used a case-sensitive severity lookup, which caused collector pods to continuously log "Invalid syslog severity value" warnings and forward logs with an incorrect default severity when using RFC 5424 keyword values such as "informational" or "Informational" in the ClusterLogForwarder syslog output. With this update, adding downcase normalization before the to_syslog_severity() call resolves the issue and administrators can configure syslog severity using case-insensitive keywords as documented
without triggering warnings.

* Invalid syslog severity value warning in collector pods while forwarding logs to a Syslog server.
* When using an RFC 5424 severity keyword (e.g., {{informational}}) in the ClusterLogForwarder syslog output, the CLF passes API validation and shows {{Valid: True}} / {{Ready: True}}, but collector pods continuously stream the following warning:

{noformat}$ oc logs collector-abcde

2026-07-01T10:51:41.466780Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Invalid syslog severity value: informational internal_log_rate_secs=1 vrl_position=2003

2026-07-01T11:02:03.677044Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Internal log [Invalid syslog severity value: informational] has been suppressed 1 times.

2026-07-01T11:02:03.677061Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Invalid syslog severity value: informational internal_log_rate_secs=1 vrl_position=2003{noformat}

* The same warning occurs with the capitalized keyword {{Informational}}:

{noformat}2026-07-01T11:03:03.301600Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Invalid syslog severity value: Informational internal_log_rate_secs=1 vrl_position=2003{noformat}

* The {{oc explain}} documentation for severity explicitly states it accepts case-insensitive keywords:

{noformat}$ oc explain clusterlogforwarder.spec.outputs.syslog.severity

  severity  <string>
    Severity values are defined in https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5424#section-6.2.1
    The value can be a decimal integer or one of these case-insensitive keywords:
        Emergency Alert Critical Error Warning Notice Informational Debug{noformat}

* Logs are forwarded to the syslog server but with a default/incorrect severity instead of the user-configured value.

* OpenShift Logging Operator version:

{noformat}$ oc get csv -n openshift-logging | grep "logging"
cluster-logging.v6.6.0                  Red Hat OpenShift Logging        6.6.0                                             Succeeded{noformat}

*How reproducible:*

Always

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Install Red Hat OpenShift Logging Operator v6.6.0
# Create a ServiceAccount and bind the required Cluster Roles:

{noformat}$ oc -n openshift-logging create serviceaccount collector
$ oc -n openshift-logging adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user logging-collector-logs-writer -z collector
$ oc -n openshift-logging adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-application-logs -z collector{noformat}

# Deploy a syslog receiver (e.g., rsyslog) accessible from the cluster on TCP/UDP port 514.
# Create a ClusterLogForwarder with a keyword severity value:

{noformat}apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1
kind: ClusterLogForwarder
metadata:
  name: collector
  namespace: openshift-logging
spec:
  managementState: Managed
  outputs:
  - name: syslog-out
    type: syslog
    syslog:
      rfc: RFC5424
      facility: user
      severity: informational                            <<=======
      url: udp://rsyslog-server.usermanaged-rsyslog.svc:514
  pipelines:
  - name: forward-to-syslog
    inputRefs:
    - application
    outputRefs:
    - syslog-out
  serviceAccount:
    name: collector{noformat}

# Verify the CLF is accepted:

{noformat}$ oc get clusterlogforwarder collector -n openshift-logging \
    -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}{.type}: {.status} - {.reason}{"\n"}{end}'

observability.openshift.io/Authorized: True - ClusterRolesExist
observability.openshift.io/Valid: True - ValidationSuccess
Ready: True - ReconciliationComplete{noformat}

# Check the collector pod logs:

{noformat}$ oc logs -n openshift-logging -l app.kubernetes.io/component=collector --tail=20 | grep "severity"{noformat}

*Current Results:*

* CLF status shows {{Valid: True}}, {{Ready: True}} -- no validation error raised.
* All collector pods continuously stream the following warning message (once per log record processed):

{noformat}$ oc logs collector-abcde

2026-07-01T10:51:41.466780Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Invalid syslog severity value: informational internal_log_rate_secs=1 vrl_position=2003

2026-07-01T11:02:03.677044Z  WARN transform{component_kind="transform" component_id=output_syslog_out_parse_encoding component_type=remap}: vrl::stdlib::log::implementation: Internal log [Invalid syslog severity value: informational] has been suppressed 1 times.{noformat}

* Also tested with capitalized keyword {{Informational}} -- same warning.
* Using numeric value {{"6"}} instead of {{informational}} resolves the warning and forwards logs with the correct severity.

*Expected Results:*

* Collector pods should not log any warning when a valid RFC 5424 severity keyword is used.
* The keyword {{informational}} (or any valid RFC 5424 keyword) should be correctly mapped to its numeric equivalent (e.g., {{informational}} -> {{6}}) in the generated syslog message.
* Logs forwarded to the syslog server should carry the correct severity as configured by the user.

*Workaround:*

Use the numeric severity value instead of the keyword in the CLF spec:

{noformat}severity: "6"    # instead of: severity: informational{noformat}

RFC 5424 severity numeric mapping:

  0 = Emergency, 1 = Alert, 2 = Critical, 3 = Error,

  4 = Warning, 5 = Notice, 6 = Informational, 7 = Debug

*Root Cause:*

If the Lokistack CR name is “lokistack” and the ClusterLogForwarder CR is “lokistack”, the:

    ...
{noformat}

h4. Description of problem:

Enabling the {{detectMultilineException}} filter in the {{ClusterLogForwarder}} fails to group multiline Java Exceptions that contain some non-nested lines after the start of the exception.

The {{Java rules}} found at the Vector source [https://github.com/ViaQ/vector/blob/v0.37.1-rh/src/transforms/detect_exceptions/rules.rs|https://github.com/ViaQ/vector/blob/v0.37.1-rh/src/transforms/detect_exceptions/rules.rs|smart-link] 
requires strict pattern matching,

The filter only detects and groups lines that both match the regex pattern and are nested/indented as per above pattern.
Certain applications emit exceptions with subsquent lines that are not nested *before the nested exceptions.*

* Vector sees this as a complete multiliine exception and flushes it prematurely.

h4. Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

OpenShift Logging 6.2.z 

OpenShift Logging 6.3.x 

h4. How reproducible:

Always

h4. Steps to Reproduce:

# Cluster has OpenShift Logging, Loki and COO installed 
# In the {{ClusterLogForwarder}} CR include a {{detecMultilineException}} filter e.g: 

{noformat}apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1
kind: ClusterLogForwarder
metadata:
  annotations:
    observability.openshift.io/log-level: debug
  name: instance
  namespace: openshift-logging
spec:
  serviceAccount:
    name: collector
  outputs:
  - name: default-lokistack
    type: lokiStack
    lokiStack:
      target:
        name: logging-loki
        namespace: openshift-logging
      authentication:
        token:
          from: serviceAccount
    tls:
      ca:
        key: service-ca.crt
        configMapName: openshift-service-ca.crt
  # INCLUDE DETECT MULTI LINE EXCEPTION FILTER
  filters:
  - name: detect-exceptions
    type: detectMultilineException
  pipelines:
  - name: default-logstore
    inputRefs:
    - application
    - infrastructure
    outputRefs:
    - default-lokistack
    # INCLUDE FILTER REF
    filterRefs:
    - detect-exceptions{noformat}
# Create a test namespace 

{noformat}oc create ns logging-test{noformat}
# Deploy the test pod simulating stack traces with alternative nesting pattern (see {{test.yaml}} file in Google Drive link in private comments)

{noformat}oc create -f test.yaml{noformat}
# Ensure pod is running and generating logs. Navigate to “Observe > Logs” in the OCP console and view each line in the exception being logged as individual events, rather than being grouped as expected.
# As a control, deploy the second test pod (see {{test-2.yaml}} file in Google Drive link in private comments). This logs a sample multi line exception which DOES correctly match the regex required by Vector to group the multiline exception.
{noformat}oc create -f test-2.yaml{noformat}
# In “Observe > Logs” observe the logs from the second test pod. The multi line  exceptions adhere to the regex pattern and are correctly grouped

*Actual results:*

Logs from pod deployed in {{test.yaml}} do not match strict regex pattern and are not grouped as expected

For comparison, logs deployed in {{test-2.yaml}}do match and are grouped correctly, proving that {{detectMultilineException}}filter is functioning.
The presence of log lines after the {{JavaStartException}} within the stack trace that are not nested, are thus not recognised as part of the stack trace. Vector terminates the grouping and the logs are flushed prematurely resulting in broken stack traces being forwarded.

h4. Expected results:

All log lines in the stack trace should be grouped and sent as a single log event.

Enabling the {{detectMultilineException}} filter in the {{ClusterLogForwarder}} fails to group multiline Java Exceptions that contain some non-nested lines after the start of the exception.

The {{Java rules}} found at the Vector source [https://github.com/ViaQ/vector/blob/v0.37.1-rh/src/transforms/detect_exceptions/rules.rs|https://github.com/ViaQ/vector/blob/v0.37.1-rh/src/transforms/detect_exceptions/rules.rs|smart-link] 
requires strict pattern matching,

The filter only detects and groups lines that both match the regex pattern and are nested/indented as per above pattern.
Certain applications emit exceptions with subsquent lines that are not nested *before the nested exceptions.*

* Vector sees this as a complete multiliine exception and flushes it prematurely.

h4. Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

OpenShift Logging 6.2.z 

OpenShift Logging 6.3.x 

h4. How reproducible:

Always

h4. Steps to Reproduce:

# Cluster has OpenShift Logging, Loki and COO installed 
# In the {{ClusterLogForwarder}} CR include a {{detecMultilineException}} filter e.g: 

{noformat}apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1
kind: ClusterLogForwarder
metadata:
  annotations:
    observability.openshift.io/log-level: debug
  name: instance
  namespace: openshift-logging
spec:
  serviceAccount:
    name: collector
  outputs:
  - name: default-lokistack
    type: lokiStack
    lokiStack:
      target:
        name: logging-loki
        namespace: openshift-logging
      authentication:
        token:
          from: serviceAccount
    tls:
      ca:
        key: service-ca.crt
        configMapName: openshift-service-ca.crt
  # INCLUDE DETECT MULTI LINE EXCEPTION FILTER
  filters:
  - name: detect-exceptions
    type: detectMultilineException
  pipelines:
  - name: default-logstore
    inputRefs:
    - application
    - infrastructure
    outputRefs:
    - default-lokistack
    # INCLUDE FILTER REF
    filterRefs:
    - detect-exceptions{noformat}
# Create a test namespace 

{noformat}oc create ns logging-test{noformat}
# Deploy the test pod simulating stack traces with alternative nesting pattern (see {{test.yaml}} file in [Google Drive link in private comments|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/LOG-9565?focusedCommentId=17408325])

{noformat}oc create -f test.yaml{noformat}
# Ensure pod is running and generating logs. Navigate to “Observe > Logs” in the OCP console and view each line in the exception being logged as individual events, rather than being grouped as expected.
# As a control, deploy the second test pod (see {{test-2.yaml}} file in [Google Drive link in private comments|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/LOG-9565?focusedCommentId=17408325]). This logs a sample multi line exception which DOES correctly match the regex required by Vector to group the multiline exception.
{noformat}oc create -f test-2.yaml{noformat}
# In “Observe > Logs” observe the logs from the second test pod. The multi line  exceptions adhere to the regex pattern and are correctly grouped

*Actual results:*

Logs from pod deployed in {{test.yaml}} do not match strict regex pattern and are not grouped as expected

For comparison, logs deployed in {{test-2.yaml}}do match and are grouped correctly, proving that {{detectMultilineException}}filter is functioning.
The presence of log lines after the {{JavaStartException}} within the stack trace that are not nested, are thus not recognised as part of the stack trace. Vector terminates the grouping and the logs are flushed prematurely resulting in broken stack traces being forwarded.

h4. Expected results:

All log lines in the stack trace should be grouped and sent as a single log event.

h4. Additional info:

See private comment for attachments

{noformat}This PR implements metrics collection profiles for ServiceMonitors, enabling cluster admins to reduce metrics cardinality by ~85% when using the minimal profile.

## What Changed

Created 6 ServiceMonitors (3 profiles × 2 components):
- Collector: `instance`, `minimal-instance`, `telemetry-instance`
- LFME: `logfilesmetricexporter`, `minimal-logfilesmetricexporter`, `telemetry-logfilesmetricexporter`

**Minimal profile**: 17 essential metrics (16 collector + 1 LFME)
- Buffer metrics: `vector_buffer_byte_size`, `vector_buffer_events`, `vector_buffer_sent_events_total`, `vector_buffer_discarded_events_total`
- Component metrics: `vector_component_received_bytes_total`, `vector_component_received_event_bytes_total`, `vector_component_received_events_total`, `vector_component_sent_bytes_total`, `vector_component_errors_total`, `vector_component_discarded_events_total`
- Events metrics: `vector_events_in_total`, `vector_open_files`
- HTTP metrics: `vector_http_client_errors_total`, `vector_http_client_requests_sent_total`, `vector_http_client_responses_total`
- Custom: `logcollector_component_event_unmatched_count`
- LFME: `log_logged_bytes_total`

**Full profile**: All ~79 vector metrics (default, no change in behavior)

**Telemetry profile**: Subset for Red Hat telemetry

## Key Technical Details

- All ServiceMonitors labeled with `monitoring.openshift.io/collection-profile: {full|minimal|telemetry}`
- TLS `serverName` parameter ensures proper verification across all profiles despite different resource names
- Profile selection via `cluster-monitoring-config` ConfigMap in openshift-monitoring namespace
- Prometheus `serviceMonitorSelector` uses `matchExpressions` with `NotIn` operator to select correct profile

h2. Context

The Loki Operator does not currently configure gRPC compression for any inter-component communication. The most impactful path is distributor to ingester, where all ingested log data flows over gRPC uncompressed. This increases network traffic, especially in multi-AZ deployments where cross-AZ data transfer adds both latency and cost.

Upstream Loki already supports {{grpc_compression}} on all gRPC client configs, with {{gzip}} and {{snappy}} as available codecs.

Beyond ingester_client, the frontend_worker gRPC client (querier → query-frontend) would also benefit from compression, as large query results flow through this path. Other gRPC clients are lower volume and lower priority.

h2.   Acceptance Criteria

* Enable {{grpc_compression}} on ingester_client.grpc_client_config in the operator generated Loki config.
* Enable compression on frontend_worker.grpc_client_config for query-path compression.
* Open a PR on [https://github.com/rhobs/rhobs-loki|https://github.com/rhobs/rhobs-loki|smart-link]  to enable the compression configuration.
* Coordinate with the RHOBS team the rolling out to Integration & Staging.
* Coordinate with the RHOBS team the rolling out to Production.
* Evaluate whether compression should be an always-on default upstream.

h2.   Developer Notes

* Ask questions if anything is not clear.
* Decide with the team if we need a separate issue for upstream
